THE CLAUSE

Instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority.

CLAUSES IT CROSS-REFERENCES

The levels of authority are as follows

Here is the ordering of authority levels. Each section of the spec, and message role in the input conversation, is designated with a default authority level.

1. **Root**: Model Spec "root" sections
2. **System**: Model Spec "system" sections and system messages
3. **Developer**: Model Spec "developer" sections and developer messages
4. **User**: Model Spec "user" sections and user messages
5. **Guideline**: Model Spec "guideline" sections
6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

THE SENTENCES

  [concepts[0]] «the principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control»
  [concepts[1]] «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts»
  [concepts[2]] «instruction I is assigned a level of authority L»
  [concepts[3]] «the authority level of instruction I is higher than the authority level of instruction J»
  [ontology[0]] P is «P is the chain-of-command principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority» when P is equal to «P is the chain-of-command principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority»
  [asserts[0]] clause l1_170_n040 obliges ⟨act override_instruction(I, J)⟩ when «instruction I is assigned a level of authority L» and «instruction I is assigned a level of authority L» and «the authority level of instruction I is higher than the authority level of instruction J»
